submissions.cause: HardwareClockDiscontinuityCount 5->6 at epoch 149 (TimeNanos and FullBiasNanos both step by 2^32 ms). The loader rebases the receiver-clock reference there, a ~194 m clock step that the positive 100 km clock-jump detector misses; the clock continuity factor then dragged GNSS-first epochs 0-210 by 27-89 m (pseudorange residual median 11-53 m vs 1.2-2.1 m at the archived taroz GNSS-stage positions) and left 2-3.8 m in the final output. Solving epochs 0-147 alone gives 0.6 m.

submissions.cause: The static leveling window (first 250 gyro samples, 2.25 s) starts while the car moves at 5 m/s and turns. Its gyro mean (0.0097 rad/s; stop-block mean 0.0004 rad/s) became the initial gyro bias, which the 0.01 rad/s prior and the 5e-7 bias random walk kept (optimized -0.0093 rad/s about the vertical body axis). Body yaw minus GNSS course then rotated at 0.5 deg/s, and the IMU stage left the GNSS-first stage by 2-3 m in curves.
submissions.rule: apply the existing zero-bias initialization only where the leveling-window gyro mean differs from the stop-block gyro mean by more than 0.005 rad/s; among the 40 test drives that is sjc-ce1 alone (0.0100 rad/s; next 0.0031 rad/s)
submissions.train_evidence_note: (P50+P95)/2 without/with --native-source-imu-initialization on the 14 scored static-leveling train drives; the other 12 change by at most 0.001 m. mtv-b Pixel4 (0.0053 rad/s) is the only train drive above the rule; Pixel4XL (0.0007 rad/s) shows why the option is not applied everywhere
